Hi Diego / Laura,

Attached is the redlined order form (v3) from our procurement team and an appendix called "IP appendix" that summarizes the request around output ownership and training exclusions. Procurement is asking for a short track to get this signed this week — they flagged a launch dependency.

Quick summary of the asks from Novalink:
- Explicit ownership of generated product output for their internal productization use (commercialization)
- Opt-out for model training on customer prompts (they want an explicit
  "no-training" carveout for our standard usage telemetry)
- A 12-month feedback license for the outputs they provide back to us for product improvements

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the above in the order form with the MSA staying as-is (we know the MSA covers broader terms)? If not, what limited carveouts/alternative language can we offer that would be approvable by legal and reasonably acceptable commercially?

Procurement also included a short checklist: revenue impact, deployment constraints, and evidence (SOC2) copy. I've attached their checklist as well.

Thanks,
Claire

Laura / Ben — looping you in early.

Thanks Claire — received. High level reaction: we should avoid assigning ownership of model weights or claiming broad ownership over the underlying service. However, Novalink's ask is focused on downstream product output and an explicit "no-training" request. Those are negotiable but have tradeoffs.

Immediate asks for the internal team:
- Laura: can you review the attached redlines and propose markups we can present (see attached "Novalink_OrderForm_v3_redlines.docx")? Key points to review are the output assignment clause and the training opt-out language.
- Ben / Monica: commercial perspective — what's the revenue sensitivity if we accept a strict training opt-out for 12 months? Does Novalink have a precedent with other vendors?

My suggested quick play: offer output license (exclusive for their productization for 12 months limited to their product lines) rather than assignment, and offer a timeboxed training opt-out (12 months) in return for slightly higher usage pricing or a commit. Also offer a 12-month, non-exclusive feedback license that allows Redwood to use anonymized outputs for product quality improvements but explicitly excludes training models on raw user data — i.e., a telemetry + aggregate-feedback license.

I'll flag this for legal prioritization. Laura, can we get a candidate mark-up by EOD tomorrow? Ben, if you can give a ballpark on price delta, I'll include that in my reply to Claire.

Thanks,
Diego

> Laura / Ben — looping you in early.
> 
> Thanks Claire — received. High level reaction: we should avoid assigning ownership of model weights or claiming broad ownership over the underlying service. However, Novalink's ask is focused on downstream product output and an explicit "no-training" request. Those are negotiable but have tradeoffs.

Thanks for the summary. I reviewed the redlines and sketched up edits in the attached MSA_Summary_Table.xlsx and the docx. High-level legal positions:

1) Output ownership: avoid language that transfers title. We can grant Novalink an exclusive, time-limited license to use generation outputs for their productization (12 months, territory: global, field: their product lines). We should include a carveout to prevent sublicensing that would effectively transfer broader rights.

2) Training opt-out: we can accept a 12-month opt-out but only for their own customer data and prompts; we must retain the right to use aggregated telemetry and de-identified signal for service quality improvements. Proposed language: "Customer Data and Outputs will not be used to train Redwood's primary model weights for 12 months; Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified feedback for model quality improvements and safety monitoring." This is clear and explains the technical limitations.

3) Feedback license: propose a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to Redwood to use feedback (annotations, error reports) for improving the service, with an explicit prohibition on using raw outputs or PII for model retraining. If Novalink insists on total prohibition, we should trade that for commercial concession.

4) Audit / evidence: procurement asked for SOC2 and data residency notes — we can provide SOC2 report and confirm data-at-rest in US region per their order form.

Open questions for commercial:
- Ben / Diego: what concession (pricing / commit) are we willing to tie to a 12-month training opt-out?

I attached the MSA_Summary_Table.xlsx with proposed redline snippets. I also added clause language suggestions in the docx.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Diego / Laura — quick commercial input.

We can accommodate a 12-month training opt-out if Novalink signs a 24-month committed spend at a ~15% uplift to the base per-token rate, or alternatively a 12-month opt-out with a smaller 8% uplift if they commit a minimum monthly spend (we should define bands). The output license (exclusive for 12 months) seems acceptable from sales if we retain restrictions on sublicensing and downstream transfer.

We should also propose a fallback: if Novalink requests complete assignment of output ownership (title transfer), we decline. Instead offer an exclusive license + an option for limited assignment of specific deliverables that both parties agree on and that pass a security review. That path would require CFO approval and is slower.

Action items I can own:
- Draft a short commercial summary (price bands, commit language) to send to Claire today.
- Prepare a one-page customer-facing summary of the legal concessions (output license, training opt-out scope, feedback license) for procurement.

If Laura gives the green light on the proposed clause language, I'll send combined redlines + commercial terms to Claire with a DocuSign request.

Ben Carter
Director, Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Novalink — proposed compromise and next steps (Order Form v3)

Claire — thanks for the patience while we pulled legal and commercial together. Below is the compromise we can move on quickly; I copied the DocuSign link at the bottom.

Executive summary (proposal):
- Output: Redwood will grant Novalink an exclusive, time-limited license to use generated outputs for Novalink's internal productization (12 months, worldwide, limited to Novalink product lines). License explicitly prohibits sublicensing that transfers broader ownership.
- Training: Redwood will accept a 12-month opt-out for using Customer Data and Outputs to train Redwood's primary model weights. Redwood retains the right to use aggregated, de-identified feedback and telemetry for quality and safety improvements only.
- Feedback: Novalink grants Redwood a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use aggregated feedback and annotations for product improvements; explicit prohibition on using raw outputs or PII for model retraining.
- Commercial: In exchange for the 12-month training opt-out, Novalink to agree to Option A: 24-month committed spend at +15% base rate, or Option B: 12-month committed spend at +8% (with minimum monthly commitment bands).

Attachments included: Novalink_OrderForm_v3_redlines.docx, MSA_Summary_Table.xlsx.

If this is acceptable, Claire, please sign the attached Order Form via DocuSign: https://docusign.com/12345NLK. If you need tighter language on any of the three buckets above, flag specifics and Laura will issue tracked changes directly in the docx.

If procurement needs additional SOC2 or region evidence, Monica can coordinate a short evidence pack.

Thanks, looking forward to closing this week.
